result: MarmoAAP enables high-throughput behavioral testing, with marmosets performing an average of 146 trials per 20-minute session (47.9 successful, 98.9 unsuccessful), representing a 15-fold increase over traditional cooperative pulling paradigms that average 10.4 trials per session.
evaluation: All reviewers explicitly affirm the high-throughput capability as a major strength. The editor notes 'clear and convincing advantages over conventional methods,' Reviewer 1 calls it 'one of the most exciting paradigms in primate social cognition to be developed in many years,' and Reviewer 2 highlights that 'typical behavioral experiments on primate cooperation provide around 10 trials per session, while using their approach the authors were able to collect over 100 trials per 20-minute session.' No reviewer questions the trial throughput data.

result: All three marmoset dyads achieved proficiency (50% success rate) in the cooperative task within a 2-month period, with an average of 33.7±11.9 training days to reach proficiency.
evaluation: The editor explicitly states that 'claims of faster social learning or of finer-grained behavioural analysis in this setup will require further corroboration.' While reviewers do not directly challenge the training data, the editor's statement indicates that claims about learning speed need additional validation beyond the proof-of-concept data presented.

result: MarmoAAP facilitates comprehensive collection of detailed behavioral data across multiple modalities, including millisecond-level lever positioning and force data, gaze dynamics through 3D head tracking, and vocalizations, with marmosets showing increased chirp calls in cooperation versus self-reward sessions.
evaluation: The editor states that 'claims of finer-grained behavioural analysis in this setup will require further corroboration.' While Reviewer 2 notes the apparatus 'appears to be highly successful at integrating behavioral data across many important contexts' and Reviewer 3 acknowledges 'the approach also supports the integration of markerless behavioral analysis,' the editor's explicit call for further corroboration indicates the fine-grained analysis claims need additional validation.

result: MarmoAAP enables wireless neural recordings during cooperative behavior, with successful isolation of single-unit activity from prefrontal cortex (OFC and dlPFC) showing increased firing rates around lever pulls, demonstrating the platform's capacity for investigating neural activity underlying naturalistic social behaviors.
evaluation: All reviewers affirm this capability without challenge. Reviewer 1 states the paradigm 'has the potential to usher in a new wave of research on the cognitive and neural mechanisms underlying primate social cognition,' Reviewer 2 notes 'the advantage of collecting neural and freely-behaving behavioral data concurrently is a significant advantage,' and Reviewer 3 confirms 'the approach also supports the integration of...neurophysiological data.' The proof-of-concept neural data is accepted as demonstrating feasibility.

result: MarmoAAP provides flexibility through adjustable task parameters (lever force, reward amount, time windows) and modular hardware design, allowing adaptation to different behaviors, individual capabilities, and various experimental paradigms including both social and non-social tasks.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently affirm the flexibility as a strength. Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'the device allows for quantitative control and adjustment to control behaviour,' and Reviewer 2 notes the apparatus 'can collect a wide range of behavioral data, with higher behavioral resolution than traditional methods.' The modular design and parameter adjustability are accepted without challenge as demonstrated capabilities.

result: The MarmoAAP apparatus consists of a modular T-slotted frame (18"h × 24"w × 18"l) with servo motor-controlled levers connected to strain gauges and potentiometers, enabling precise control of lever force and position with different success criteria for Self-Reward versus Mutual Cooperation conditions.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 explicitly commends the authors, stating 'the device is well-described, and the authors should be commended for their efforts in both designing this system but also in "writing it up" so that others can benefit from their R&D.' Reviewer 2 confirms 'the authors provide substantive information about the design of the apparatus.' No reviewer questions the technical specifications or apparatus design.

result: DeepLabCut2 multi-animal tracking was used to track six facial features on both marmosets, trained on 270 frames for 15,000 iterations, with Anipose used for 3D reconstruction of head frames from three synchronized cameras.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 notes the paradigm allows 'precisely quantifying their visual behavior (e.g. gaze)' and Reviewer 3 confirms 'the approach also supports the integration of markerless behavioral analysis.' The technical details of the tracking implementation are not challenged by any reviewer.

result: Seven adult marmosets (3 males, 4 females; 6.0±1.7 years) were trained using familiar cage-mate pairs with minimal food/water restriction (1-3 hr), using marshmallow-water rewards and progressive training through decreasing cooperative time windows (3s to 1s).
evaluation: The experimental methods and subject details are accepted without challenge by all reviewers. Reviewer 1 states 'the manuscript was well written and provided sufficient details for others to adopt this paradigm,' and Reviewer 3 notes the work meets the criteria to 'describe the approach and instrumentation' and 'show the feasibility of use.' No concerns are raised about the training protocol or animal welfare procedures.

result: Marmosets are presented as an ideal primate model due to their small size, prosocial nature, genetic proximity to humans, cooperative breeding behavior, advanced socio-cognitive abilities, and neural similarities to humans in social cognition circuits.
evaluation: The editor describes this as a 'valuable study' for marmosets as 'an increasingly popular primate model for neuroscience.' Reviewer 1 notes the authors 'leverage the many advantages of this primate model for studies of social brain functions,' and Reviewer 3 states 'the marmoset stands as a great platform to study primate social cognition.' The rationale for using marmosets is accepted without challenge.

result: Traditional cooperative pulling paradigms have limitations including low behavioral resolution, manual coding constraints, frequent experimenter intervention, and low trial throughput (averaging 10.4 trials per session across species), failing to fully capture nuances of marmoset social interactions.
evaluation: All reviewers implicitly accept these limitations as justification for the new apparatus. Reviewer 1 notes 'the classic pull task...has several key limitations' and that 'it has not been feasible to adopt the task for neuroscience experiments.' The comparison data on traditional paradigm throughput is used by reviewers without challenge to contextualize the improvement.

result: Neural recording methods involved head chamber implant, craniotomy, 64-channel linear array electrode with nanodrive, 20 kHz sampling, and spike sorting using Kilosort2 and phy to isolate single and multi-units.
evaluation: The neural recording methodology is accepted without challenge. Reviewer 2 notes 'the strength of evidence is solid in terms of the ability of the apparatus to perform as described' and Reviewer 3 confirms the approach 'supports the integration of...neurophysiological data.' The technical details are treated as standard methodology.

result: MarmoAAP bridges the gap between traditional animal behavior methodologies and modern demands for precision and adaptability, balancing naturalistic behavior with controlled experimental paradigms.
evaluation: The editor calls this a 'valuable study' with 'clear and convincing advantages,' Reviewer 1 describes it as 'an elegant illustration of how naturalistic questions can be adapted to more rigorous experimental paradigms,' and Reviewer 3 confirms the work successfully meets the goals of a methods paper. The overall contribution is affirmed by all reviewers.
